b8de0e4d474e76c982a415968858fca44f1e540b.summary: CrowdStrike reports a cryptojacking campaign it calls Kiss-a-dog that targets exposed Docker and Kubernetes environments. Attackers used a host mount to escape containers, mined with XMRig through anonymous pool servers, and hid processes with kernel and user-mode rootkits. They also removed cloud monitoring agents, scanned for exposed Docker and Redis instances, and left a Redis backdoor. The report says the tools and techniques were previously associated with TeamTNT.

b818769367968b7a26a16612fe7133e70fa7b7c7.summary: Dark Reading reports that UK and US retailers are seeing help-desk password-reset calls linked to Scattered Spider, an English-speaking cybercrime group also tracked as UNC3944. It cites the Dior breach on May 7, which took customer data from China and South Korea, and notes that Google Threat Intelligence Group flagged a shift to US retailers. The group is described as financially motivated, using phishing and credential abuse to deploy ransomware or steal data. The report says the group's role in retail attacks claimed by DragonForce is unclear, and that alleged members have been arrested.
